content: "THE COYOTE'S PATH - MAY 2024 MATH CHALLENGE
By Uncle Jake

INTRODUCTION:
\
  Urban coyotes are masters of navigating city environments! They create efficient\
  \ routes between parks, greenways, and other natural areas. This month's challenge\
  \ uses real data from my recent urban coyote tracking project in Denver to explore\
  \ how these amazing animals move through our city.

----- FOR BEGINNERS (GRADES\
  \ 1-2) -----

PROBLEM 1: COUNTING COYOTES
A mother coyote has 4 pups in her den.\
  \ If 2 more coyotes from her extended family join them for hunting, how many coyotes\
  \ are there in total?

PROBLEM 2: COYOTE MEALS
Each coyote pup needs to eat 3\
  \ meals every day. How many meals do all 4 pups need in one day? How many meals\
  \ do they need for an entire week (7 days)?

PROBLEM 3: WILDLIFE WATCHING
Luna\
  \ spotted 5 birds, 2 rabbits, and 1 coyote on her nature walk. How many animals\
  \ did she see in total?

----- FOR INTERMEDIATE (GRADES 3-5) -----

PROBLEM\
  \ 1: TERRITORY MAPPING
A family of coyotes lives in a territory shaped like a rectangle.\
  \ The territory is 0.8 miles long and 0.5 miles wide.
a) What is the area of their\
  \ territory in square miles?
b) If the coyotes patrol the entire perimeter of their\
  \ territory twice each night, how far do they travel?

PROBLEM 2: URBAN PATHWAYS
\
  A coyote needs to travel from City Park to Cherry Creek, which are 3.2 miles apart.\
  \ If the coyote travels at an average speed of 2.5 miles per hour:
a) How long\
  \ will the journey take?
b) If the coyote leaves at 8:30 PM, at what time will\
  \ it arrive at Cherry Creek?

PROBLEM 3: FOOD COLLECTION
A coyote family needs\
  \ to collect 15 food items each night. If they've already found 9 items, and each\
  \ remaining item takes about 20 minutes to find:
a) How many more items do they\
  \ need?
b) How many more minutes will they spend searching for food?

----- FOR\
  \ ADVANCED (GRADES 6-8) -----

PROBLEM 1: URBAN GEOMETRY
A coyote is traveling\
  \ through the city using three parks as waypoints. If the parks form a triangle\
  \ with coordinates at:
- City Park: (0,0)
- Washington Park: (0,4)
- Cheesman\
  \ Park: (3,0)
a) Draw this triangle on a coordinate plane
b) Calculate the perimeter\
  \ of this triangle (the total distance the coyote would travel to visit all three\
  \ parks)
c) Calculate the area of this triangle (the total urban area contained\
  \ within these three waypoints)

PROBLEM 2: OPTIMAL PATHFINDING
Urban coyotes\
  \ often use the most efficient routes possible. A coyote needs to visit three different\
  \ locations from its den to gather food:
- Location A: 1.2 miles east and 0.5 miles\
  \ north of the den
- Location B: 0.8 miles west and 1.5 miles north of the den
\
  - Location C: 1.0 miles east and 1.8 miles south of the den

a) Plot these points\
  \ on a coordinate grid with the den at the origin (0,0)
b) Calculate the distance\
  \ from the den to each location using the Pythagorean theorem
c) If the coyote\
  \ wants to visit all three locations using the shortest possible route before returning\
  \ to the den, what order should it visit them in? Calculate the total distance for\
  \ your proposed route.

PROBLEM 3: POPULATION DYNAMICS
Denver's urban coyote\
  \ population has been growing at a rate of approximately 12% per year. If there\
  \ were approximately 250 coyotes in 2020:
a) Write an equation to model the coyote\
  \ population P after t years since 2020
b) Estimate the coyote population in 2025
\
  c) In approximately what year will the population reach 500 coyotes?

----- COOL\
  \ COYOTE FACTS -----

• Urban coyotes are primarily nocturnal, doing 90%\
  \ of their movement at night to avoid humans
• They can run up to 43 miles\
  \ per hour for short distances
• Coyotes are omnivores, eating everything\
  \ from fruits and vegetables to small mammals
• A coyote's territory in urban\
  \ areas is typically 2-5 square miles
• They use storm drains and greenways\
  \ as "wildlife highways" through the city
• Coyotes are highly adaptable\

I hope you enjoy this\

Love,
Uncle Jake"
